vendors.name: Zluri
vendors.specialist_in: SaaS management + access lifecycle / access reviews; mid-market to enterprise. Discovery via 9 methods (SSO, finance, browser agent, direct integrations, HRIS, desktop agent, etc.), license optimization, automated on/offboarding playbooks, access certification campaigns.
vendors.included_because: Pure-play SMP leader; deepest access-review/compliance surface among SMP vendors (UAR campaigns), strong app-discovery and offboarding automation. Anchors the compliance column.

vendors.name: Torii
vendors.specialist_in: SaaS management for mid-market; discovery, spend/renewal tracking, no-code workflow automation for on/offboarding, shadow-IT detection, contract repository.
vendors.included_because: Flagship pure-play; strong workflow-automation surface and renewal/contract tracking. Mid-market relevant.

vendors.name: Josys
vendors.specialist_in: SaaS + DEVICE management converged for SMB/mid-market (50-250 users sweet spot). App discovery, license management, on/offboarding, AND hardware/device inventory + assignment. Explicit IT-suite convergence.
vendors.included_because: Directly central to the user's 'ERP for IT, 50-250 users' question: ships SaaS + device + lifecycle in one. Evidence of downward convergence into ITAM/hardware.

vendors.name: Setyl
vendors.specialist_in: IT asset + SaaS + spend management for SMB/mid-market. App & license register, hardware asset register, vendor/contract management, spend tracking, on/offboarding workflows, GL/accounting integration.
vendors.included_because: 50-250-user specialist that fuses SaaS, hardware, contracts, and spend; strongest evidence of the SaaS-to-IT-suite convergence the audit asks about. Anchors contract/spend column.

vendors.name: BetterCloud
vendors.specialist_in: SaaS operations + security: automated user lifecycle (on/mid/offboarding), least-privilege/access automation, file/data security policies, SaaS configuration drift, deprovisioning evidence.
vendors.included_because: Defines the automation + data-deprovisioning/offboarding-evidence surface; strongest least-privilege and DLP-adjacent compliance entities.

vendors.name: Productiv
vendors.specialist_in: SaaS intelligence: deep feature-level engagement analytics, app rationalization, license right-sizing benchmarks, renewal intelligence, app portfolio.
vendors.included_because: Best-in-class usage/engagement-analytics and benchmarking surface; informs optimization entities.

vendors.name: Zylo
vendors.specialist_in: Enterprise SaaS management + SaaS spend/renewal intelligence; system of record for SaaS contracts, renewals, spend, benchmarks. Finance-led.
vendors.included_because: Defines the spend/contract/renewal-as-system-of-record surface and benchmark data; anchors spend + renewal column.

missing.reason: User-access-review (certification) campaigns are a first-class object in Zluri and BetterCloud and the primary SOX/SOC2 access-governance artifact in SMP. No current entity captures a campaign header.
Per-grant approve/revoke certification decisions; the line-item evidence backing each access-review campaign. Absent.

All flagship vendors model an offboarding execution record (per-departing-user run with per-app revocation steps and outcome). smp_workflow_runs is generic; a dedicated offboarding/joiner-mover-leaver run with evidence is the compliance artifact. Could be modeled as a typed view of smp_workflow_runs, but vendors treat it as its own object.

Immutable per-app data-deprovisioning / data-deletion evidence record (account deactivated, data exported/deleted, license reclaimed, timestamp, actor). Required for GDPR erasure proof and SOX. No current entity.

The entitlement-state object: user x app x role/permission currently provisioned. Distinct from smp_license_seat_assignments (commercial seat) - this is the access-governance fact and the subject of every access review. Present in Zluri/BetterCloud/Torii. Missing.

Discovery-method/connector registry (SSO, finance feed, browser/desktop agent, HRIS, direct API). Zluri markets 9 discovery methods; the source is a tracked, configured object with coverage/confidence. smp_app_integrations covers app-to-app integrations, not the discovery channels feeding the inventory.

An organization's account/tenant within a SaaS app (org may hold multiple tenants/workspaces of one app). Vendors distinguish the app (product) from the discovered account/instance carrying users, spend, contracts. Missing - users and spend currently attach directly to saas_applications.

Plan/edition/seat-type catalog per app (e.g. Free/Pro/Enterprise, full vs light seat). Right-sizing recommendations compare assigned tier vs usage. Present in Zluri/Productiv/Zylo. No current entity holds the tier definition.
Finance-sourced invoice/transaction lines reconciled to subscriptions; the raw spend artifact behind smp_spend_allocations. Zylo/Setyl/Torii ingest invoices as a discrete object. Missing.
Functional-category taxonomy used for rationalization/redundancy analysis (e.g. two project-management apps). Lightweight config; present across vendors. Missing as an explicit entity.
Feature-level engagement events powering Productiv-style deep usage analytics; finer grain than saas_usage_metrics aggregates. Specialist; lower priority.
Installment/billing-schedule rows for multi-year or quarterly contracts; used in spend forecasting. Specialist (Zylo/Setyl). Lower priority.
Least-privilege role/permission profiles per app used by access policies and reviews. Specialist (Zluri/BetterCloud). Lower priority; may be deferred.

boundary_checks.note: Per audit brief, the following are sibling/umbrella domains, NOT SMP gaps. No SMP MISSING was raised for them.

ITAM/SAM - NOTE: convergence observation, see commentary; Josys/Setyl ship this but it is not SMP-owned in this catalog

out_of_scope_correctly_excluded.owner: IGA - SMP consumes identity for discovery+access but does not master the IdP

modularization.module_floor_check: PASS - 4 full modules, each with >=1 required master; domain has >=3 capabilities so >=2 modules satisfied (Rule #14).
modularization.assessment: The 4-module split (Discovery, Renewal/Vendor, Optimization, Automation) maps cleanly to the four jobs-to-be-done a first-time deployer would recognize: find the apps, manage the money/contracts, right-size the licenses, and run the access/request workflows. Each module self-explains. The principal coverage gap is not the SPLIT but the DEPTH of SMP-AUTOMATION: it currently carries only workflow plumbing (workflows, runs, requests) and lacks the access-governance/compliance evidence layer (reviews, grants, offboarding runs, deprovisioning logs) that every flagship now treats as core. That is a MISSING-entity gap inside an otherwise correctly-scoped module, not a modularization defect.

recommendations.reason: Split is coherent and onboarding-legible. Keep as-is.

OPTIONAL/commentary only. If the 5 access-governance compliance entities (access_reviews, access_review_items, access_grants, offboarding_runs, deprovisioning_logs) are added, the module's scope broadens from 'automation' to 'access governance + automation'. A rename would keep the name honest. Not required; do not act without user sign-off.

convergence_observation.headline: Modern SMP vendors are extending DOWN into hardware, contracts, and unified spend - converging toward an integrated 'ERP for IT' suite, especially at the 50-250-user tier.
evidence: Josys ships SaaS management AND hardware/device inventory + assignment in one product, explicitly targeting SMB/mid-market.
Setyl fuses SaaS + hardware asset register + vendor/contract management + spend (with GL/accounting integration) for the same segment.
Zluri, Torii, Zylo have all added contract repositories and finance-fed spend tracking, pulling renewal/contract/invoice data SMP historically did not own.
The 50-250-user buyer wants ONE tool for apps + devices + contracts + spend + on/offboarding, not four point tools - this is the 'ERP for IT' shape.
convergence_observation.implication_for_catalog: SMP's current surface DOES capture the renewal/contract and spend-tracking entities (saas_subscriptions, legal_contracts embedded_master, smp_spend_allocations, smp_renewal_*, smp_vendor_*), so the contract/spend convergence is already reflected. The entities SMP does NOT and should NOT own (per the boundary rules) are hardware_assets/device_inventory (ITAM/SAM) and the cross-asset unified contract master (ITAM umbrella). The convergence is therefore a CROSS-DOMAIN composition story (SMP + ITAM + SAM + FINOPS surfaced as one suite), not a reason to expand SMP's footprint into hardware. Recommend treating 'ERP for IT' as a suite/bundle composition over these sibling domains rather than a scope expansion of SMP. This is commentary, not a gap.
convergence_observation.in_scope_convergence_gaps: Within SMP's correct boundary, the convergence does justify deepening spend granularity (smp_vendor_invoices, smp_payment_schedules) and discovery breadth (smp_discovery_sources, smp_app_accounts) - these are listed as MISSING above and ARE SMP-owned.
